text:
maria: Heads-up, acme POC blocked on auth. They hit embeddings and get 401 "Invalid API key" after we handed over demo credentials. Sample they sent: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-demo-abc123" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Project: acme-poc" \n  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
rahul: Quick sanity checks: is that key active in the key-store and which region did they call? 401 typically means key unknown/disabled. 403 would be permission/project mismatch.

maria: Customer says they saw 403 briefly when they didn't include the project header, then switched and got 401. They also use a corporate proxy that rewrites hosts to us-west-2 for compliance.

infra-bot: log: [2025-11-12T15:02:34Z] key=sk-acme-demo-abc123 action=auth-check result=not-found region=eu-central

leo: infra-bot shows the key exists in eu-central not us-west-2. If their proxy routes to us-west-2 and the key was created in eu-central, auth will fail. Two fixes: update their proxy or create a key in the region they call.

maria: Can we ask them to run `curl -I` so we can see headers and the upstream host? Also we have an internal debug endpoint to show key metadata if they can call it (we asked them to mask secrets):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-demo-abc123" https://internal.redwood/debug/key-binding
```
This will print `key_id`, `bound_org`, `bound_projects`, `scopes`, `region`.

rahul: Also confirm they aren't accidentally rotating to a short-lived token (service account JWT) that expired. That would surface as 401 too.

maria: Customer pasted `curl -I` output showing Host: api.redwood.ai but their proxy rewrote DNS to api.us-west-2.internal, so yeah it's going to us-west-2.

leo: I'm going to create a short-lived presales key bound to acme-poc in us-west-2 so they can continue. Command (admin):
```bash
redwoodctl keys create --org acme --project acme-poc --scopes embeddings --region us-west-2 --label "acme presales temp"
```
I'll send the new key via secure channel.

infra-bot: log: [2025-11-12T15:04:50Z] key=sk-acme-demo-xyz789 action=create owner=leo region=us-west-2 bound_projects=["acme-poc"]

maria: Sent new key. Customer retried and reports 200 + embeddings payload. :tada:

olga: Great! Small deal note: they asked about rate limits and sustained throughput pricing for embeddings (they expect 150k calls/day). Can we capture expected RPS and demonstrate Dedicated/volume pricing? @maria please capture numbers and I'll draft pricing addendum.

maria: Will capture TPS and weekly volume. Another Q from security questionnaire: how can they rotate/revoke programmatically? I referenced our docs but they want a single-line API snippet we can paste.

leo: For internal/presales answer: revoke is admin-only `DELETE /v1/keys/{key_id}` on the control plane, authenticated with admin service token. For customers we provide a UI and support-assisted revocation for presales keys. Example (no creds):
```bash
curl -X DELETE https://control.redwood.ai/v1/keys/sk-acme-demo-xyz789 \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>"
```
Followed by `POST /v1/keys` to create replacement.

rahul: Follow-ups: 1) rotate and revoke old sk-acme-demo-abc123 2) update acme repo to show region selection or use api.redwood.ai with explicit region header 3) olga to prepare pricing note 4) add short revocation snippet to presales playbook.

maria: Done on our side, customer greenlit evaluation. Closing thread.
